title: Say what will be learned, then teach
statement: Early in a teaching script, state what will be learned as one testable sentence and go straight into teaching; a hook or topic label doesn't count.
example: The target sentence must come within about the first 30% of the script, and an opening hook does not count.
detail: The video-script check asks for an orientation beat: one sentence that states the learning target as a testable proposition, in the first ~30% of the script, followed straight away by teaching rather than a multi-step roadmap or a series of questions (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`). A sentence that only names a topic fails, and so does a script whose first substantive statement is a hook, unless a clear orientation beat also appears within the first 30%.
against: The rationale is uncited: 'cognitive load research is unambiguous that learners encode better when they know the learning target before the details arrive.' (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`, line 201). The hook-versus-target line is also the one distinction that still flipped after the judge was made more consistent: 'genuine rubric ambiguity — the opening hook vs orientation-beat distinction' (`shadow-bench`, git commit bfc4165, line 19).

evidence.quote: - One sentence that explicitly states the learning target as a testable proposition
- Must appear in the first ~30% of the script
- Immediately followed by teaching (not by a multi-step roadmap or a series of questions)
If the first substantive statement is a hook, the script fails proposition_clarity unless a clear orientation beat also appears within the first 30%.
- "Today we're going to learn about cells and what makes them special." → Describes a topic, not a testable proposition.
cognitive load research is unambiguous that learners encode better when they know the learning target before the details arrive.
genuine rubric ambiguity — the opening hook vs orientation-beat distinction

evidence.path: sources/Othello Unit Video_ Info Sheet for Devfactory.md
evidence.quote: Every sentence carries knowledge. No puzzle hooks, rhetorical teasers or openings that are only atmosphere.
